correctness.rationale: The edge-root spans at an articulation form a direct sum; affine invariance permits product coordinates. With block dimensions a,b the free-sum primal volume gains a!b!/(a+b)!, canceled by normalization; the polar is a Cartesian product. A bridge contributes one. On a cycle the signed edge differences identify the polar with the central section of the cube [-1,1]^n, with absolute determinant n on the zero-sum hyperplane. Coarea gives polar volume 2^(n−1)f_n(n/2)/√n for the [0,1]-uniform sum density, and inclusion–exclusion gives the stated finite density sum. For odd n the polar vertices have one zero coordinate and balanced remaining signs, giving simplicial primal facets. For even n they are balanced sign vectors; the resulting facet's unique affine dependence equates the positive- and negative-side barycenters. Subtracting the smallest positive-side convex coefficient from all that side's coefficients and adding it on the other side gives the stated triangulation, with disjoint interiors. Every simplex cone uses a signed path-root basis of Gram determinant n. This yields the stated primal volume and the product including the listed small factors. The density's sinc integral has relative correction −3/(20n); expansion near zero with Gaussian domination and exponentially small off-center contribution gives relative O(n^−2). Stirling supplies −1/(4n) for even n and +1/(4n) for odd n in the rescaled binomial, hence −2/5 and +1/10 in the product.
residual_risks: The finite hull checks are approximate and are not used as proof. The large-n expansion is for one cycle factor, not a uniform asymptotic over cacti as their total order grows. The result does not claim monotonicity at every cycle length.

evidence: Alexander et al. describe the ℓ1-sum for one-point gluing and the biconnected decomposition. Bartha et al. give the central diagonal section formula and expansion including relative terms −3/(20n) and −13/(1120n²). D’Alì et al. give polar Ehrhart information via cuts/flows. Ohsugi–Tsuchiya's cactus theorem at p. 2 is for the graph suspension.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general gluing result specializes to cactus blocks immediately, and the stronger central-section expansion transfers through the elementary cycle difference map. The related Ehrhart cut/flow and suspension results need not by themselves state this product.

evidence: Known one-point gluing plus known primal h* and central section formulas give every exact factor. In terms of I_n, the central volume for the unit-side cube, the factor is √n I_n times the normalized binomial b_n. The earlier I_n expansion already has the relative coefficient −3/20 at order 1/n.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Multiply I_n by the standard expansion of √n b_n, whose correction is −1/4 when n is even and +1/4 when n is odd; the respective sums are −2/5 and +1/10. The only coordinate bridge for the polar is the invertible consecutive difference map with image the zero-sum hyperplane. Neither the parity coefficient nor the complete block product requires a substantive new estimate or new volume information.
searches: Alexander et al., arXiv:1911.10642, p. 2 and Theorem 3.3

evidence: The cycle polar is the zero-sum cube section in consecutive potential-difference coordinates. The earlier graph Lipschitz-free paper treats the primal and polar in this general language. In the same-day slab record §3, W_n(t)t tends to 2n binom(n−1,floor((n−1)/2))/n!, and V_n(t)/t tends to 2^n f_n(n/2) with f_n for uniforms on [0,1].
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Scale the slab's normal coordinate by 1/t; the body converges to the central cube section times a segment. Indeed the rescaled body lies between products of the segment with section scalings 1−t/n and 1+t/n. Normalized volume product is unchanged by the segment factor and is polar-invariant. Thus the slab's normalized limiting product equals the normalized cycle product; the two limits stated in §3 give exactly the same binomial–density factor. There is no same-day priority inference.

evidence: The assigned record is an exact self-hit, not separate prior work. Ohsugi–Tsuchiya display the cycle gamma-polynomial with coefficients binom(2i,i); Kálmán–Tóthmérész reproduce cycle Ehrhart data. The earlier Lipschitz-free paper explicitly covers the four-cycle equality.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The Ehrhart h* value at one is normalized primal volume. With the stated gamma coefficients it is 2^(n−1) times Σ_{i≤floor((n−1)/2)}binom(2i,i)/4^i; telescoping the sum gives n binom(n−1,floor((n−1)/2)). Thus lack of a separately indexed exact Mahler table does not leave the primal or the joint numbers uncovered.

originality.rationale: The exact cactus formula follows by simple block multiplication of known primal cycle data and known central cube section volumes, related to the cycle polar by the signed edge differences. The apparent remaining contribution, the parity correction, is also the direct product of the already published section expansion (which includes even its n^−2 term) and standard central-binomial Stirling estimates. An inspected distinct same-day slab record also supplies the exact normalized cycle factor as its thin-slab limit. That comparison is equivalent coverage, not evidence of ordering; the originality rejection rests on the direct implications of the earlier primary sources.
residual_risks: No historical claim about who first wrote the final combined formula or the same-day slab comparison is made. Earlier coverage is through the stated geometrical identification and direct multiplication of the verified primary-source components.

value.rationale: Cactus blocks and diagonal cube sections are natural objects, and the formula is a useful synthesis. Under this scope, however, no independently useful unknown exact fact remains: the patching of blocks and all numerical and asymptotic input are already supplied by known gluing, Ehrhart, central-section and binomial formulas. The work does not add a classification of new extremizers, a global parity monotonicity theorem, or even a new central-section estimate that could constitute a separate finding.
residual_risks: No judgment against future cactus-volume or cycle-extremal results is implied. No substantive repaired finding was established.
